offered_action_specs.name: rollback_deploy
offered_action_specs.description: Roll one service back to the settings it ran before its latest deploy, as the deploy log records them. Code plans it from that log, not from your tools' results, so you can name it even when they cannot see deploys: if the log holds no deploy of that service to undo, or the service changed since, code refuses it. Its container is recreated, so the service pauses while it restarts. Money already booked wrong stays wrong: a rollback stops new damage, and repairs nothing.

first_checks: Check the ledger-consumer process: is it running, restarting, or stuck? Read its logs around 20:30-20:42 for errors, repeated retries of one message, or a poison event it cannot book.
Read the ledger consumer group's lag and committed offsets on provider-events per partition: is the lag growing, flat (stuck), or shrinking (slow)?
Compare with the payment-confirmer group's lag on the same topic: if it is also behind, the problem is upstream or in Kafka, not in the ledger.
Check PostgreSQL for the ledger: locks, long transactions, failed inserts or constraint violations (e.g. unbalanced double entry) that would block or fail bookings.
Check webhook-receiver and the produce rate into provider-events for a sudden burst that could explain a backlog that is only temporary.
triage.if_false: The alert is false if the ledger group's committed offsets reach the topic's end offsets up to the cutoff (lag 0) and a fresh money check settles: then the 15 s wait was only a transient burst, or the lag metric came from a stale or wrong consumer group.

proposed.why: No tool calls are left; the evidence points to one event the ledger consumer retries forever, which blocks it.

findings.cause: One provider event, evt_000282 (Kafka provider-events partition 1, offset 129, key pay_000256), carries an amount that the consumers reject: 'amount must be positive integer cents'. ledger-consumer was recreated at 20:41:22 with BAD_EVENTS=retry. Because of that setting it does not skip the event. It retries the same message forever, with the backoff growing to 15 s. Its offset on partition 1 never moves past 129. Since about 20:42:16 it has also stopped posting anything on any partition, so the whole consumer is stalled, not just that one partition. The ledger group's lag therefore grows on all partitions (about 177 in total at 20:42:35), and the money check cannot settle up to its cutoff, which raises BooksBehindProvider. payment-confirmer got the same event. It runs with BAD_EVENTS=dead_letter, so it dead-lettered the event and kept going.

evidence.shows: Consumer lag (no group label) was 0 on all 3 partitions at 20:40:35, then 8-9 at 20:41:35 and 55-62 at 20:42:35: a growing lag, not a stale metric.
ledger-consumer was recreated at 20:41:22 with LEDGER_HANDLER=idempotent and BAD_EVENTS=retry. All the other services date from 20:39:56. payment-confirmer has BAD_EVENTS=dead_letter.

ledger-consumer logs 'could not book; will retry the same message' for provider-events/1＠129, attempts 3 to 10 from 20:41:26 to 20:42:40, error 'amount must be positive integer cents', with the backoff capped at 15 s.
payment-confirmer dead-lettered the same message, provider-events/1＠129, at 20:41:24 with the same amount error.

The trace shows evt_000282 queued by webhook-receiver to partition 1 at offset 129. payment-confirmer's outcome is dead_lettered. ledger-consumer has 10 or more spans, all with error and will_retry, spread over at least 60 s.
webhook-receiver logged evt_000282 as queued at 20:41:24, with key pay_000256 and a valid signature path. The log lines do not show the amount.
The ledger's 'posted' rate falls from about 3.6/s to 0 by 20:42:31, while payment-confirmer keeps processing at about 3/s. The ledger consumer as a whole has stopped making progress.

findings.left_open: The actual amount in evt_000282 is not known: it may be zero, negative, fractional, or in the wrong unit. Also open is why the provider sent it, and whether it relates to pay_000256. payments-api logged nothing for pay_000256 in the last 10 minutes (c7), so where that payment came from is open. The metrics do not settle whether the event is a provider-side oddity or a charge we sent with a bad amount; payments-api has CHARGE_AMOUNT_UNIT=cents. It is also unconfirmed why the retry on one partition stops booking on partitions 0 and 2. A single-threaded consumer that blocks while sleeping would explain it, but no tool showed this. No money_check was run, so whether anything beyond the lag is wrong (missing or double postings) is unverified. Note that the ledger consumer's redeploy at 20:41:22 changed BAD_EVENTS to retry, and the event arrived at 20:41:24, about 2 s after the redeploy.

why: the investigator's report: passed to the fixer

proposed.why: The logs, trace and metrics agree that ledger-consumer is stuck retrying one bad message, provider-events/1@129, under BAD_EVENTS=retry, and has stopped booking; no further tool is needed to name the cause and a safe fix.

diagnosis.hypothesis: Event evt_000282 (key pay_000256, provider-events partition 1 offset 129) arrived at 20:41:24 with an amount both consumers reject ('amount must be positive integer cents'). ledger-consumer had been recreated at 20:41:22 with BAD_EVENTS=retry, so it retries that message forever with backoff capped at 15 s and never commits past 1@129. Its ledger 'posted' rate fell to zero shortly after, so it stopped booking on every partition, not just 1. The tools do not show why; a blocking sleep in a single consumer loop is a plausible guess. Its lag grows, and the money check cannot settle to its cutoff, which raises BooksBehindProvider. payment-confirmer, on BAD_EVENTS=dead_letter, dead-lettered the event and kept going. The event's actual amount, its origin, and the ledger's settings before 20:41:22 are not known.

evidence.shows: ledger-consumer logs 'could not book; will retry the same message' for provider-events/1@129, attempts 3 to 10, from 20:41:26 to 20:42:40. Error: 'amount must be positive integer cents'. retry_in_seconds goes 2, 4, 8, then 15 each time after.

Trace of evt_000282: webhook-receiver queued it to partition 1 offset 129. payment-confirmer's outcome is dead_lettered. ledger-consumer has 9 spans (not 10 or more, as the report says), all error/will_retry, from 0 to about 60.5 s.

ledger-consumer was recreated at 20:41:22 with LEDGER_HANDLER=idempotent and BAD_EVENTS=retry, 2 s before the bad event. Every other service dates from 20:39:56. payment-confirmer runs BAD_EVENTS=dead_letter. The result does not show the ledger's settings before 20:41:22.
payment-confirmer dead-lettered provider-events/1@129 at 20:41:24.705 with the same amount error. This is its only ERROR/WARN line in 5 minutes.

The ledger 'posted' rate (1m window) falls from about 3.6/s at 20:41:16 to 0.16 at 20:42:16 and 0 from 20:42:31, so booking stopped about 20:41:30 to 20:42:00. payment-confirmer keeps about 3/s throughout. The whole ledger consumer is stalled.

Lag is 0 on partitions 0, 1 and 2 at 20:40:35, 8-9 at 20:41:35, and 55-62 (177 in total) at 20:42:35. The series carry no group label, so the group is inferred, not shown. Since the confirmer keeps up, the lag is most likely the ledger's.
webhook-receiver logged evt_000282 as queued at 20:41:24.702 with key pay_000256 at partition 1 offset 129. The log does not show the amount.
payments-api logged nothing for pay_000256 in the last 10 minutes, so the payment's origin is open.

proposed_fix.summary: Recreate ledger-consumer with BAD_EVENTS=dead_letter, keeping LEDGER_HANDLER=idempotent, so it dead-letters 1@129 and drains the backlog on all partitions. Then inspect evt_000282 in the dead letters to learn its amount and whether it is a provider oddity or our bad charge. Repair or book pay_000256 by hand, since neither consumer has booked or confirmed it. Run the money check afterwards. I name no fix_action: rollback_deploy would restore the pre-20:41:22 settings, which no tool showed. That rollback could also change LEDGER_HANDLER away from idempotent and risk double postings.

diagnosis.blast_radius: ledger-consumer pauses while it is recreated, and the lag grows briefly. With dead_letter, any other bad events also go unbooked into dead letters, leaving gaps the money check must flag. Booking about 180 backlogged events at once is safe only with the idempotent handler kept. evt_000282's money stays unbooked until it is repaired by hand.
diagnosis.rollback_plan: Recreate ledger-consumer with its current settings (LEDGER_HANDLER=idempotent, BAD_EVENTS=retry). The committed offsets stay as they are; dead-lettered events can be replayed from the dead-letter store once they are fixed.
